33	Turns the speech in clips into captions, on this Mac or with AssemblyAI, and places them as text clips on a new track of their own at the front. It does what [**File ▸ Generate Captions…**](/captions/generate-captions/) does.
34	
35	The new clips are [ordinary text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/), so they draw in the preview, in `render_frame` and in an export, and they can be retimed with `move_clip` or restyled with `set_text`.
36	
37	**Arguments**
38	
39	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
40	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
41	| `clips` | array of integers | No | Transcribe only these clips, at least one. Left out, every clip with recorded sound in the timeline or nest that's open. |
42	| `engine` | string | No | `apple` (the default) on this Mac, or `assemblyai` in the cloud. See [Transcribe engines](#transcribe-engines). |
43	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`. On this Mac it defaults to the Mac's own language. With AssemblyAI it defaults to `auto`, which detects the language. |
44	| `style` | string | No | `subtitles` (the default), `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. See [Caption styles and paging](#caption-styles-and-paging). |
45	| `place` | boolean | No | True (the default) places the cues as one undo step. False answers the cues and changes nothing. See [Check a transcript before placing it](#check-a-transcript-before-placing-it). |
46	| `replace` | boolean | No | With a word style, removes earlier caption tracks in the same undo step. See [Restyle captions](#restyle-captions). |
47	| `slide` | boolean | No | The pill slides between words. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
48	| `fill` | boolean | No | The spoken word fills from left to right. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
49	| `dim` | boolean | No | The page fades in a pause. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
50	| `speakers` | boolean | No | AssemblyAI only. Ask who says what. Default false. See [Speakers and vocabulary](#speakers-and-vocabulary). |
51	| `vocabulary` | array of strings | No | AssemblyAI only. Words and phrases to expect. See [Speakers and vocabulary](#speakers-and-vocabulary). |
52	| `refresh` | boolean | No | AssemblyAI only. Ignore the kept transcript and upload again. Default false. |
53	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
54	
55	Only a clip playing a movie or sound file can be transcribed, and not one played in reverse, whose words would come out backwards. A clip you name that can't be is listed under `skipped`. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
56	
57	**What it answers**
58	
59	| Key | What it holds |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| `cues` | The cues, placed or not, each with `start`, `end` and `text`. With a word style each also has `words`, a list of `start`, `end` and `text` in timeline ticks, and `size` where a lone word shrank. |
62	| `engine`, `language` | The engine that ran and the language it used. |
63	| `clips_read` | The clips words came from. |
64	| `placed` | Whether the cues were placed. |
65	| `captions` | How many text clips were placed. |
66	| `track_name` | The name of the new track. |
67	| `trimmed` | How many cues were shortened to meet the next one, when any were. |
68	| `replaced` | The ids of the tracks removed, whenever `replace` was given. |
69	| `looks` | The looks that were on, whenever `slide`, `fill` or `dim` was given. |
70	| `skipped` | Each clip that gave no captions and why, when there are any. |
71	
72	A placed run also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary. Subtitles cues are at most two lines of 42 characters and at most 6 s, with a frame between them.
73	
74	An AssemblyAI run adds these:
75	
76	| Key | What it holds |
77	| --- | --- |
78	| `uploaded` | The media files sent. |
79	| `cached` | The media files answered from the transcript kept in the project, with no request. |
80	| `audio_seconds` | The seconds of audio billed. |
81	| `speech_model_used` | Each uploaded file's `media` and `model`. |
82	| `language_detected` | With `language` left out or `auto`, each uploaded file's `media`, `code` and, when AssemblyAI gave one, `confidence`. |
83	| `endpoint` | The host the run's requests went to. Absent when no key is set. |
84	| `note` | Anything else worth saying: a cut vocabulary, a fallback model, a delete AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed, or a transcript that couldn't be kept for reuse. |
85	
86	**When it refuses**
87	
88	Nothing changes and nothing is uploaded when:
89	
90	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
91	- Nothing has recorded sound. The answer reads "Nothing in this timeline has recorded sound to transcribe…", or, for clips you named, "None of those clips can be transcribed" with the reason for each.
92	- `style` or `engine` isn't one of its spellings. The answer names them all.
93	- `speakers`, `vocabulary` or `refresh` is given with engine `apple`. Giving one at all is enough, even as false.
94	- `replace` is given with `subtitles` or with `place: false`. Giving it at all is enough, even as false.
95	- `slide`, `fill` or `dim` is true with a style it doesn't show on, or with `place: false`.
96	- The `language` tag is misspelt, for engine `apple`. The answer lists the tags speech recognition knows, 24 at most.
97	- The language is real but its speech model isn't on this Mac, for engine `apple`. The answer lists the languages ready here, 24 at most. This is a separate answer from a misspelling, because a person has to fix it: they open **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, choose the language and press **Download**. The tool never downloads a model. See [Download a speech language](/captions/on-device-transcription/#download-a-speech-language).
98	- No AssemblyAI key is set and a file needs uploading: "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."
99	- The project has nowhere to keep its transcripts, which is rare: "This document has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first."
100	
101	Once a run starts, a clip that fails is listed under `skipped` and the others are still placed. That includes a clip whose file is over AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit, and a clip where no speech was heard. The exception is a key AssemblyAI refuses, which ends the run with nothing placed, because every later file would fail the same way. If no cues come out of the whole run, nothing is placed and the answer says why, for example "No speech was recognised in the audio that was transcribed."
102	
103	If an AssemblyAI run fails after it has spent money, the answer says so: "AssemblyAI had already been billed for 1 media file (N audio seconds) before this failed." [When a file fails](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#when-a-file-fails) lists the reasons you can see.
104	
105	### Transcribe engines
106	
107	**`apple`** is the default. Speech recognition runs on this Mac and nothing leaves it. It needs no permission and has no length limit. Each run recognises the audio again, because this engine keeps nothing for `transcribe` to reuse, and `refresh` doesn't apply.
108	
109	Speech models are installed per Mac, from the **Download** row in **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. `language` matches a tag such as `en-US`, a language's display name, or a bare code such as `en`, which takes the first matching language on this Mac.
110	
111	**`assemblyai`** sends the audio of every media file behind the clips you named to AssemblyAI, a cloud service that bills for it. It sends the whole file, not only the parts in use. The transcript is deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
112	
113	:::caution
114	Don't choose `assemblyai` for somebody else's recording without their say-so. Audio leaves the Mac and the owner of the key pays for it.
115	:::
116	
117	- **The engine is never remembered.** Left out, it's `apple`, whatever the sheet last chose. An agent that wants the cloud says so on every call.
118	- **Each file is kept.** One transcript per media file is kept in the project package, so a second run over the same files with the same settings makes no request and lists them under `cached`. See [Reuse a transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript).
119	- **`refresh`** ignores what's kept and uploads again, and the file is billed again.
120	- **The key.** A new transcription needs your AssemblyAI key. A run whose every file already has a current transcript needs no key and makes no network request, unless `refresh` is true.
121	- **`language`.** `auto`, the default, detects the language and the answer reports it. Any other code goes to AssemblyAI unchecked, and one it doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.
122	- **The region.** It's a choice in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/), and no argument sets it. `endpoint` tells you where a run's requests went.
123	
124	The built-in Assistant can't use this engine. A call with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld from it, and it points you to **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).
125	
126	### Speakers and vocabulary
127	
128	Both need `engine: "assemblyai"`. The sheet's rows are described on [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#split-the-words-by-speaker).
129	
130	`speakers: true` asks AssemblyAI who says what, and a change of speaker then starts a new cue. With `subtitles`, each speaker's cues take their own colour: white, yellow, cyan, then green in order of first appearance, then round again. A speaker is a label within one media file, so one person in two files can come back as two speakers.
131	
132	`vocabulary` tells AssemblyAI the words and phrases to expect, such as product names, people and identifiers. Terms are trimmed, repeats are dropped keeping the first spelling, and the list stops at 1,000 terms. `note` says so when it was cut.
133	
134	### Check a transcript before placing it
135	
136	`place: false` answers the cues and changes nothing, with no edit and no undo step. Use it to read a transcript before committing to it.
137	
138	`replace` and any look set to true are refused with it, because nothing is placed. To place the captions, call again without `place`. With AssemblyAI the second call reuses the kept transcript and uploads nothing.
139	
140	### Caption styles and paging
141	
142	`style` chooses how the words look. It's the same choice as **Style** in the sheet, and the default is never what the sheet last chose. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
143	
144	| `style` | What it makes |
145	| --- | --- |
146	| `subtitles` | Two-line cues in the Caption preset. The default. |
147	| `highlight` | Montserrat Black, upper case, the word being said in yellow with a pop. |
148	| `pill` | Montserrat ExtraBold, upper case, the word being said on a violet pill. |
149	| `karaoke` | Montserrat ExtraBold as written, up to two lines, words turning yellow. |
150	| `build` | Anton, upper case, words appearing one by one. |
151	| `one_word` | Bebas Neue, one large word at a time. |
152	
153	Every style but `subtitles` is a word style, and makes pages rather than cues. Each page holds its words' timings, so the word being said is drawn as the style says.
154	
155	A page is filled to the width it will measure on this canvas in that style, at most 0.86 of the canvas width, not to a word count. It sits on one line, or up to two with `karaoke`. A page also closes at:
156	
157	- a change of speaker
158	- a gap of 0.25 s or more
159	- a word ending in `.`, `?`, `!` or `…`
160	- 3 s on screen
161	
162	A lone word too wide for the canvas shrinks, down to 80 % of the style's size, before it wraps. Pages stay inside their own clip. A page meets the next one where the gap is under 0.25 s, and otherwise holds for 0.5 s after its last word.
163	
164	### Caption looks
165	
166	`slide`, `fill` and `dim` add a look to a word style's pages, as the sheet's three boxes do. Each is false unless given, and never what the sheet last chose. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/).
167	
168	| Argument | The sheet's box | What it does | Works with |
169	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
170	| `slide` | **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the word before to the word being said, over 0.2 s or sooner, instead of jumping. | `pill` |
171	| `fill` | **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken, taking 0.6 s at most. | `highlight`, `karaoke`, `build` |
172	| `dim` | **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more. | All five word styles |
173	
174	True is refused by name with any other style, or with `place: false`, where it would show nothing. False is always accepted. Words from engine `apple` rarely carry a pause that long, so `dim` shows mostly with `assemblyai`.
175	
176	Whenever one of the three was given, a placed run lists under `looks` the ones that were on.
177	
178	### Restyle captions
179	
180	To change a word style, run `transcribe` again with `replace: true`. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
181	
182	`replace` removes, in the same undo step, every track this command could have made over these clips: a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The answer lists those tracks under `replaced`.
183	
184	It needs a word style and `place` true. A style is only a display choice, so with AssemblyAI a kept transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, and restyling uploads nothing. Engine `apple` recognises the audio again.
185	
186	## `import_captions`
187	
188	Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file and lays it out as text clips, one for each cue, on a new track of its own. It does what [**File ▸ Import Captions…**](/captions/import-captions/) does, and that page has what the reader copes with.
189	
190	They're ordinary text clips in the Caption preset, so they burn in on export with no further step. Times snap to the frame grid, and a cue that overlapped the next one is shortened to meet it.
191	
192	**Arguments**
193	
194	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
195	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
196	| `path` | string | Yes | The absolute or `~` path to the `.srt` file. |
197	| `track` | integer | No | Put the captions on this existing track instead of a new one, which the menu can't do. Cues that would overlap something there are dropped, so it's safer to leave this out. |
198	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
199	
200	**What it answers**
201	
202	| Key | What it holds |
203	| --- | --- |
204	| `cues` | How many cues survived. |
205	| `captions` | How many text clips were made. It's smaller than `cues` when a track you named turned some away. |
206	| `track_name` | The new track's name. Absent when you named a track. |
207	| `trimmed` | How many cues were shortened, when any were. |
208	| `skipped` | Every entry it couldn't read or place, with its line number, when there are any. |
209	
210	It also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary. It's one undo step, **Import Captions**.
211	
212	**When it refuses**
213	
214	Nothing changes when there's no file at `path` ("No file at …"), when `track` names no track, when the file can't be read as text, when not one cue in it can be read, when a track you named takes none of the cues, or when it would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. [When a file can't be read](/captions/import-captions/#when-a-file-cant-be-read) has the sentences.
215	
216	## `export_captions`
217	
218	Writes one text track out as a subtitle file, one cue for each text clip, at the time it sits at and in the order they play. It does what [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) does. It edits nothing and makes no undo step.
219	
220	**Arguments**
221	
222	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
223	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
224	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, for example `~/Movies/talk.srt`. The folder must exist. A trailing `.srt` or `.vtt` is replaced by the format's own. Any other extension stays as part of the name, so `chart.png` becomes `chart.png.srt`. |
225	| `format` | string | No | `srt` (SubRip) or `vtt` (WebVTT). By default the path's own extension when it's one of those, otherwise `srt`. A format you name wins over the path's extension. |
226	| `track` | integer | No | The track to write. Leave it out when exactly one track holds only text clips. |
227	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
228	
229	**What it answers**
230	
231	`path` (the file really written, which can differ from what you asked for), `format`, `track`, `track_name`, `cues` (how many were written) and the `project` summary.
232	
233	**When it refuses**
234	
235	The track is never guessed, because writing the wrong track and reporting success is worse than asking. Nothing is written when:
236	
237	- No track holds only text clips.
238	- Several do and `track` is left out. The answer lists each candidate by id and name, front-most first. Call again with `track`.
239	- `track` names no track, holds a clip that isn't text, or has no caption text on it.
240	- The folder doesn't exist, or the file can't be written.
241	
242	The built-in Assistant asks you before it runs this tool, because it writes a file.
243	
244	**Round trips.** Exported and brought back with `import_captions`, every cue returns to the tick it was written from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match one you first imported. See [Frame-exact round trips](/captions/export-captions/#frame-exact-round-trips).
245	
246	## `relay_captions`
247	
248	Pages word captions again for the current canvas, from the words their pages hold, so every correction is kept. It does what [**File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**](/captions/re-lay-captions/) does, and it's the step to take after `set_canvas`.
249	
250	It looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** holding only text clips, in the timeline or in the open nest at the nest's size. A track whose pages are all in one of the five word styles, with its looks, is paged again and put back at the same place in the stack, with the same name, hidden and locked as before. It's one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
251	
252	**Arguments**
253	
254	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
255	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
256	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
257	
258	**What it answers**
259	
260	| Key | What it holds |
261	| --- | --- |
262	| `relaid` | Each track paged again: `track` (the new track), `replaced` (the old one), `name`, `style` and `pages`. |
263	| `kept` | Each track left as placed: `track`, `name` and `reason`. |
264	
265	It also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary.
266	
267	A track is kept when it's a matte track, holds a page with no word timings (Subtitles pages included), holds a page none of whose words starts inside it, holds a page in a style Frame Job doesn't make, has pages in more than one style, or wouldn't fit the project's clip limit. [Tracks kept as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) explains each reason.
268	
269	**When it refuses**
270	
271	With nothing it can re-lay, nothing changes and the answer begins "relay_captions found no caption track it can re-lay:", followed by each kept track and its reason, or "there is no track named Captions holding only text clips".
272	
273	## `get_transcript`
274	
275	Answers one clip's spoken words with their times on the timeline, ready for `ripple_delete_ranges`. The Assistant uses it to [cut a false start](/cleanup/false-starts/). No menu item shows these words clip by clip. The nearest view is the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), which [`get_timeline_transcript`](#get_timeline_transcript) mirrors. It edits nothing, makes no undo step and never uploads anything.
276	
277	**Arguments**
278	
279	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
280	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
281	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip whose words to read, in its own timeline position and speed. |
282	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. A kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
283	| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's start by default. See [The from and to window](#the-from-and-to-window). |
284	| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
285	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
286	
287	**What it answers**
288	
289	| Key | What it holds |
290	| --- | --- |
291	| `words` | The words sorted by start, each with `text`, `start`, `end` and `filler`, and `speaker` where the transcript labelled it. |
292	| `count` | How many words came back. |
293	| `engine` | `assemblyai` for a kept transcript, or `apple` for this Mac's recogniser. |
294	| `language` | The language of the words, when known. |
295	| `fillers_reported` | Whether the transcript was made with filler words. See [Fillers in a transcript](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
296	| `cached` | With engine `apple`, whether the answer came from what was already heard. |
297	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
298	| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
299	| `note` | Anything to know: no words were heard, fillers may be missing, or word starts haven't been moved yet. |
300	| `project` | The project summary. |
301	
302	**When it refuses**
303	
304	- The clip doesn't exist, or it has no words to read: "Clip 3 has no words to read: its audio is switched off." The reason can also be that it isn't a media file, plays in reverse, has no audio track, or that its file is missing.
305	- The window is empty, or outside the clip.
306	- The `language` tag is misspelt. The answer lists the tags speech recognition knows, 24 at most.
307	- There's no kept transcript and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one. A person installs it from **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
308	- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.
309	
310	### Where the words come from
311	
312	The words come from the file's current AssemblyAI transcript, kept in the project, when it has one. That transcript comes from an earlier AssemblyAI run, such as [`transcribe`](#transcribe) or the sheet. Otherwise this Mac's own speech recogniser runs over the clip, which takes seconds per minute of speech. Reading never uses the network and needs no key.
313	
314	- **Where a word starts.** An on-device word's start is moved to where its sound begins, using the file's voice detection and waveform. The recogniser's own start is often early, inside the pause before the word. Until voice detection has finished with the file, starts are the recogniser's and `note` says so, so ask again once it has. AssemblyAI words and every word's end are as transcribed.
315	- **Saved for next time.** What the recogniser heard is saved in the project for each media file and language. A later request inside a stretch it has heard comes back at once, even from another clip of the same file at another speed, and `cached` says so. It's used only while the media file and the macOS version are unchanged.
316	- **Speed.** Words are placed through the clip's speed, including a speed ramp, so their times match what plays on the timeline.
317	- **Language.** On-device recognition uses this Mac's language unless `language` names another.
318	- **Stopping.** The Assistant's **Stop** ends a long on-device read, and nothing is saved from a stopped read.
319	
320	### Fillers in a transcript
321	
322	`filler` is true for um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with punctuation at their edges trimmed.
323	
324	`fillers_reported` says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all. It's false for every on-device read, and for a kept transcript made without them. A filler can then be in the audio and missing from `words`, and `note` says so. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).
325	
326	### The from and to window
327	
328	`from` and `to` are timeline times, and they return only the words that overlap that part of the timeline. A word crossing an edge comes back whole, with its own times.
329	
330	Either end can be given alone. A missing `from` is the clip's start and a missing `to` is its end. The window is held inside the clip and echoed back as `from` and `to`. An empty window, or one wholly outside the clip, is refused.
331	
332	With a window, the on-device recogniser hears only that part and 2 s either side.
333	
334	## `get_timeline_transcript`
335	
336	Answers every word heard on the timeline, or inside the open nest, in timeline order, with nested clips included. Each word carries the range the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) would cut it by. It edits nothing, makes no undo step, never makes a network request and needs no key.
337	
338	**Arguments**
339	
340	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
341	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
342	| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's start by default. A word across this edge comes back whole. |
343	| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
344	| `tracks` | array of integers | No | Only the words playing on these timeline tracks. Every track by default. |
345	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. Each language is kept apart, and a kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
346	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
347	
348	**What it answers**
349	
350	| Key | What it holds |
351	| --- | --- |
352	| `words` | Each word, ordered by start, then end, then the front track first. Its keys are below. |
353	| `count` | How many words are on this page. |
354	| `pauses` | Each pause. See [Cut words and pauses](#cut-words-and-pauses). |
355	| `media` | Each file read, with `media`, `engine`, `language` and `fillers_reported`. |
356	| `no_words` | Clips that can't be read, each with `clip`, `nest_path`, `tag` and `reason`. |
357	| `notes` | Sentences to read: the same speech twice, words not transcribed with fillers, or word starts not moved yet. |
358	| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
359	| `truncated`, `next_from` | Present when there's more. See [Paging](#paging). |
360	| `project` | The project summary. |
361	
362	Each word has these keys:
363	
364	| Key | What it holds |
365	| --- | --- |
366	| `text`, `start`, `end` | The word and its timeline times. |
367	| `clip`, `track`, `media` | The clip it comes from, the timeline track it plays on and its media file. A nested word's track is its nest clip's. |
368	| `engine` | `assemblyai` or `apple`. |
369	| `filler` | True for a [filler word](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
370	| `speaker` | The speaker, when the transcript labelled one. |
371	| `editable`, `why` | Whether cutting it is safe, and why not when it isn't. |
372	| `id` | The word's identity across edits. |
373	| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | The range the Transcript tab cuts this word by. |
374	
375	**When it refuses**
376	
377	- `to` isn't after `from`, or the window is wholly outside the timeline.
378	- A `tracks` id names no track.
379	- The `language` tag is misspelt.
380	- A file needs this Mac's recogniser and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one.
381	- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.
382	
383	### Heard words and editable words
384	
385	Words come from every clip that plays speech from a media file, clips inside nests included. A clip that's muted, soloed out or at volume 0 isn't heard and gives no words.
386	
387	A clip whose words can't be read is listed under `no_words` with the reason instead: its audio switched off, played in reverse, or its file missing, for example.
388	
389	`editable` is false, with a sentence in `why`, for a word:
390	
391	- inside a nest. Open the nest with `set_scope` and read again to cut words inside it.
392	- under a transition, where a cut would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour.
393	- on a locked track, where a cut would leave the word in place and move everything after it.
394	
395	`id` names a word across edits elsewhere on the timeline. It has four parts:
396	
397	| Part | What it is |
398	| --- | --- |
399	| `nest_path` | The nest clips the word plays through. |
400	| `media` | Its media file. |
401	| `source` | Its start in the media's own time, in ticks, as the recogniser put it. |
402	| `k` | How many earlier words have the same three, which is 0 unless one piece of the file plays twice. |
403	
404	### Read once per file
405	
406	Each file without a current AssemblyAI transcript is read whole by this Mac's recogniser the first time it's needed, at about 0.7 s per minute of speech on an M2 Max. The words are saved in the project, so a later call answers at once.
407	
408	Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file, or reading again later doesn't read the file again. The saved words are used while the file and the macOS version stay the same. The Assistant's **Stop** ends a read, and nothing is saved from a stopped read. The Transcript tab's own **Stop** leaves an agent's read running. See [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/).
409	
410	An on-device word's start is moved to its sound as in [`get_transcript`](#where-the-words-come-from), and `notes` names any file still waiting for voice detection.
411	
412	### Duplicate speech
413	
414	When two clips of different files carry the same speech at the same time, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, `notes` names the pair and both sets of words stay in `words`. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read the speech once.
415	
416	### Paging
417	
418	At most 2,000 words come back in one answer. When there's more, `truncated` is true and `next_from` says where to call again. Pass it as `from`.
419	
420	A word overlapping that point can come back again on the next page, with the same `id`, so match words by `id`. A pause is listed on the page that holds the word before it.
421	
422	### Cut words and pauses
423	
424	`cut_start` and `cut_end` are the range the Transcript tab cuts a word by when it alone is deleted, snapped to frames. The range runs from where the word's sound starts to where the next word's sound starts, at most 1 s past the word's end, widened over any other track's word it would cut into. See [Where a word cut falls](/captions/delete-words/#where-a-word-cut-falls).
425	
426	To cut a run of words, call `ripple_delete_ranges` once, with one range from its first word's `cut_start` to its last word's `cut_end`. Check that each word is `editable` first. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
427	
428	Each row of `pauses` is a silence over 1 s between two words of one clip, read from voice detection:
429	
430	| Key | What it holds |
431	| --- | --- |
432	| `start`, `end` | Where the silence runs. |
433	| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | What the Transcript tab cuts when the pause is deleted, with 0.2 s kept at each end, snapped to frames. |
434	| `clip`, `track`, `media` | Where it is. |
435	| `follows`, `precedes` | The ids of the words before and after it. |
436	
437	To shorten a pause, call `ripple_delete_ranges` with `[[cut_start, cut_end]]`. Not every silence is listed. See [When a pause isn't shown](/captions/shorten-pauses/#when-a-pause-isnt-shown).
438	
439	Everything after a cut moves, so read the transcript again before the next one. The ids still name the same words.
440	
441	## Related
442

445	- [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/)

1	---
2	title: "Tools: reading analysis"
3	description: Read what Frame Job finds in a file or clip, from hard cuts and faces to people, sounds and person masks, and check on Remove Background.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These two tools hand an agent what Frame Job finds in your media. `get_media_analysis` reads shots, faces, people, sounds and person masks for a file or a clip. `analyze_cutout` makes a cut-out clip's masks and says where they stand.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Remove Background', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background"
13	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'analyze_cutout']}
14	  needs="Nothing. Both run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	Neither tool edits anything or makes an undo step. Results are kept for each media file in the project's cache, so a part that's been analysed answers at once. Times are in ticks, 600,000 to a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) explains the analysis itself.
18	
19	## `get_media_analysis`
20	
21	Answers an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays. No menu item shows these results as numbers. **View ▸ Show Subjects** [draws](/framing/show-subjects/) the selected clip's faces and subjects at the playhead, from what's already been found, and never starts an analysis itself.
22	
23	**Arguments**
24	
25	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
26	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
27	| `kind` | string | Yes | What to find: `shots`, `masks`, `faces`, `sound_events` or `subjects`. |
28	| `media` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | The media file to analyse. |
29	| `clip` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | A media clip. Its file is analysed over the part the clip plays. |
30	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in the file's own time played forwards, in ticks, not snapped. The file's start, or the start of the part the clip plays, by default. |
31	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in the file's own time. The file's end, or the end of the part the clip plays, by default. Must be after `from`. |
32	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
33	
34	`from` and `to` are file times, not timeline times. They're held inside the file, and with `clip` they're held inside the part the clip plays.
35	
36	**What it answers**
37	
38	Every kind answers these, as well as its own keys below:
39	
40	| Key | What it holds |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| `kind`, `media` | What was asked for and the file it was read from. |
43	| `clip` | The clip, when you named one. |
44	| `from`, `to` | The window that was read. |
45	| `size` | The media's upright picture size, as width and height. |
46	| `cached` | True when the answer came from the cache alone. |
47	| `stamp` | What the cache was made with. |
48	| `run` | Present only when this call ran the analysis: `queued_at`, `started_at` and `ended_at`, in seconds of the app's uptime. |
49	| `project` | The project summary. |
50	
51	With `clip`, each cut, sample or window also has `clip_time`, in ticks from the clip's start in its playing direction, through its speed, ramp and reversal, and `timeline`, the clip's start plus `clip_time`.
52	
53	**When it refuses**
54	
55	- You named both `media` and `clip`, or neither.
56	- `kind` isn't one of the five. The answer lists them.
57	- A media or clip id names nothing, or the clip isn't a media clip, so it has no media to analyse.
58	- A picture kind is asked of a file with no moving picture, which includes a still image: "Media 4 has no moving picture, so it has no shots to find."
59	- `sound_events` is asked of a file with no sound, or of a clip that plays in reverse, whose sound runs backwards.
60	- The file is missing. `relink_media` points it at the file.
61	- `to` isn't after `from` once both are held inside the file or the clip.
62	- The analysis fails, or the Assistant's **Stop** ends it.
63	- The kept results can't be read. The answer says which cache files to remove so they're made again.
64	
65	### Long analyses and big answers
66	
67	A call waits at most 60 s. After that it stops and says how much of the window was covered, for example "The faces analysis of media 2 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." What was covered is kept, so another call carries on from there.
68	
69	An answer over 512 KiB of cuts, runs, samples or windows is refused, and the sentence names the largest `to` that fits. So read a long file in `from` and `to` windows:
70	
71	| Kind | One row | One answer holds |
72	| --- | --- | --- |
73	| `faces` | About 176 bytes with one face, 221 with `clip` | About 296 s of samples, 236 s with `clip`, and less with more faces in frame. Read about 2 minutes at a time. |
74	| `subjects` | About 177 bytes with one person and one salient box, 222 with `clip` | About 294 s of samples, 235 s with `clip` |
75	| `sound_events` | About 130 bytes | About an hour of windows |
76	
77	### `kind: shots`
78	
79	Finds the hard cuts. It answers `count` and `cuts`, sorted by time. Each cut has `frame`, the file's frame index, and `source`, its time in the file.
80	
81	- A cut inside a gradual dissolve isn't reported.
82	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
83	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
84	
85	`split_at_shots` cuts clips at these moments. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/).
86	
87	### `kind: masks`
88	
89	Finds a person's outline in every frame and answers where a person is, never the masks themselves.
90	
91	| Key | What it holds |
92	| --- | --- |
93	| `mask_size` | The masks' own width and height. |
94	| `frames` | How many frames in the window have been analysed. |
95	| `subject_found` | Whether any frame holds a person. |
96	| `count` | How many runs there are. |
97	| `runs` | Each run of consecutive frames that agree, with `from`, `to`, `subject_found` and `frames`, in the file's own time. |
98	
99	A frame holds a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. `runs` have no `clip_time` or `timeline`, even with `clip`.
100	
101	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) draws these masks. A still picture's masks aren't this tool's. Use [`analyze_cutout`](#analyze_cutout) for those.
102	
103	### `kind: faces`
104	
105	Finds every face at 10 samples a second of the file's own time. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
106	
107	| Sample key | What it holds |
108	| --- | --- |
109	| `source` | The sample's instant in the file. |
110	| `frame` | The time of the frame it read, the first at or after `source` within one sample, or null. |
111	| `faces` | Each face in the sample. |
112	
113	| Face key | What it holds |
114	| --- | --- |
115	| `box` | `[x, y, w, h]`, from 0 to 1 of the upright picture, measured from its top-left corner. |
116	| `confidence` | How sure the detection is. |
117	| `roll`, `yaw` | How far the face is tilted and turned, in radians. |
118	| `mouth_gap` | The inner lips' height, over the face box's height. |
119	| `mouth_width` | The outer lips' width, over the face box's height. |
120	
121	`mouth_gap` over `mouth_width` is how open the mouth is. Values are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where no value was found.
122	
123	Faces are ordered from left to right and carry no identity or name. To follow one, follow its box from sample to sample.
124	
125	### `kind: subjects`
126	
127	Finds people and the regions the eye is drawn to, at 10 samples a second. Every sample instant is also a `faces` sample. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
128	
129	Each sample has `source` and `frame`, as `faces` does, then `people` and `salient`. Both are lists of `box` and `confidence`, with boxes measured as faces' are and ordered from left to right, with no identity. A person box covers the head and shoulders. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/).
130	
131	### `kind: sound_events`
132	
133	Listens to the file's first sound track with Apple's Sound Analysis, in windows of 1.5 s that start every 0.75 s, and says how sure it is of six kinds of sound: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It needs a file with sound, and an audio file works.
134	
135	| Key | What it holds |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| `window`, `hop` | The window's length and the step between windows, in ticks: 900,000 and 450,000. |
138	| `groups` | Each kind of sound, with `name`, `labels` (the classifier's labels it's the highest confidence of), `first_class` and `threshold`. |
139	| `count` | How many windows came back. |
140	| `windows` | Each window, with `source`, its start in the file, and a confidence from 0 to 1 for each of the six kinds. |
141	
142	Confidences are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where a window runs past the end of the sound.
143	
144	:::note
145	These are hints, never a finding on their own. `first_class` is false and `threshold` is null for all six.
146	:::
147	
148	## `analyze_cutout`
149	
150	Says where Remove Background stands for cut-out clips and makes their masks now. It's the agent's version of **Status** and [**Analyze Now**](/effects/remove-background/#analyze-now) in the Clip tab's **Picture ▸ Background** section.
151	
152	A cut-out clip is one whose `set_video` `cutout` is set, which is what **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the section's checkbox do. A clip's masks are made as soon as that's set, so an agent needs this tool only to wait for them or to read how they went. A still picture counts, and its one frame is made from the picture itself.
153	
154	A call asks for every frame the clips play and runs again an analysis that failed or was stopped. Frames already analysed are never analysed again. It then waits up to `wait` seconds for every clip to settle, and it never refuses for time: call again to keep waiting. The Assistant's **Stop** ends the wait.
155	
156	**Arguments**
157	
158	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
159	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
160	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The cut-out clips to answer for. Left out, every cut-out clip in the timeline or nest that's open, in timeline order. |
161	| `wait` | number | No | How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, from 0 to 60. Left out, it's 0, which answers now. |
162	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
163	
164	**What it answers**
165	
166	`clips`, a row for each clip, and the `project` summary. Each row has these keys:
167	
168	| Key | What it holds |
169	| --- | --- |
170	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
171	| `state` | Where it stands. See the next table. |
172	| `progress` | From 0 to 1. |
173	| `quality` | The clip's cutout quality, `standard` or `best`. |
174	| `frames` | How many frames of the file the clip plays, which is 1 for a picture. |
175	| `covered` | How many of those are analysed. |
176	| `ready` | Whether `covered` equals `frames`. |
177	| `subject_found` | Whether a subject was found. |
178	| `centroid` | `x` and `y`, the subject's mean centre over those frames, in the media's upright pixels from the top left with y going down. Null unless the state is `ready`. The app doesn't show this figure. |
179	| `error` | With `failed`, the sentence saying why. |
180	
181	| `state` | What it means | The app's **Status** |
182	| --- | --- | --- |
183	| `analyzing` | The masks are being made. | **Analyzing N %** |
184	| `ready` | Every frame is analysed, and a person, or a picture's foreground subject, was found. | **Ready** |
185	| `no_person` | Every frame is analysed and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. | **No person found** |
186	| `no_subject` | A picture with subject `foreground` has no subject, so it draws whole. | **No subject found** |
187	| `failed` | The masks couldn't be made. | **Failed:** and the reason |
188	| `no_picture` | The clip plays no frame of its file. | **No picture to analyze** |
189	
190	Every state but `analyzing` counts as settled.
191	
192	**When it refuses**
193	
194	Nothing is done when:
195	
196	- `wait` is outside 0 to 60: "wait must be from 0 to 60 seconds."
197	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
198	- A clip you named has no Remove Background: "Clip 3 has no Remove Background; set_video `{cutout: {}}` turns it on."
199	- With `clips` left out, no clip in the open timeline or nest has it on.
200	
201	## Related
202	
203	- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
204	- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
205	- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
206	- [Tools: picture and grade (set_video)](/mcp/tools-set-video/)

18	
19	## `get_media_analysis`
20	
21	Answers an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays. No menu item shows these results as numbers. **View ▸ Show Subjects** [draws](/framing/show-subjects/) the selected clip's faces and subjects at the playhead, from what's already been found, and never starts an analysis itself.
22	
23	**Arguments**
24	
25	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
26	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
27	| `kind` | string | Yes | What to find: `shots`, `masks`, `faces`, `sound_events` or `subjects`. |
28	| `media` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | The media file to analyse. |
29	| `clip` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | A media clip. Its file is analysed over the part the clip plays. |
30	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in the file's own time played forwards, in ticks, not snapped. The file's start, or the start of the part the clip plays, by default. |
31	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in the file's own time. The file's end, or the end of the part the clip plays, by default. Must be after `from`. |
32	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
33	
34	`from` and `to` are file times, not timeline times. They're held inside the file, and with `clip` they're held inside the part the clip plays.
35	
36	**What it answers**
37	
38	Every kind answers these, as well as its own keys below:
39	
40	| Key | What it holds |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| `kind`, `media` | What was asked for and the file it was read from. |
43	| `clip` | The clip, when you named one. |
44	| `from`, `to` | The window that was read. |
45	| `size` | The media's upright picture size, as width and height. |
46	| `cached` | True when the answer came from the cache alone. |
47	| `stamp` | What the cache was made with. |
48	| `run` | Present only when this call ran the analysis: `queued_at`, `started_at` and `ended_at`, in seconds of the app's uptime. |
49	| `project` | The project summary. |
50	
51	With `clip`, each cut, sample or window also has `clip_time`, in ticks from the clip's start in its playing direction, through its speed, ramp and reversal, and `timeline`, the clip's start plus `clip_time`.
52	
53	**When it refuses**
54	
55	- You named both `media` and `clip`, or neither.
56	- `kind` isn't one of the five. The answer lists them.
57	- A media or clip id names nothing, or the clip isn't a media clip, so it has no media to analyse.
58	- A picture kind is asked of a file with no moving picture, which includes a still image: "Media 4 has no moving picture, so it has no shots to find."
59	- `sound_events` is asked of a file with no sound, or of a clip that plays in reverse, whose sound runs backwards.
60	- The file is missing. `relink_media` points it at the file.
61	- `to` isn't after `from` once both are held inside the file or the clip.
62	- The analysis fails, or the Assistant's **Stop** ends it.
63	- The kept results can't be read. The answer says which cache files to remove so they're made again.
64	
65	### Long analyses and big answers
66	
67	A call waits at most 60 s. After that it stops and says how much of the window was covered, for example "The faces analysis of media 2 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." What was covered is kept, so another call carries on from there.
68	
69	An answer over 512 KiB of cuts, runs, samples or windows is refused, and the sentence names the largest `to` that fits. So read a long file in `from` and `to` windows:
70	
71	| Kind | One row | One answer holds |
72	| --- | --- | --- |
73	| `faces` | About 176 bytes with one face, 221 with `clip` | About 296 s of samples, 236 s with `clip`, and less with more faces in frame. Read about 2 minutes at a time. |
74	| `subjects` | About 177 bytes with one person and one salient box, 222 with `clip` | About 294 s of samples, 235 s with `clip` |
75	| `sound_events` | About 130 bytes | About an hour of windows |
76	
77	### `kind: shots`
78	
79	Finds the hard cuts. It answers `count` and `cuts`, sorted by time. Each cut has `frame`, the file's frame index, and `source`, its time in the file.
80	
81	- A cut inside a gradual dissolve isn't reported.
82	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
83	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
84	
85	`split_at_shots` cuts clips at these moments. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/).
86	
87	### `kind: masks`
88	
89	Finds a person's outline in every frame and answers where a person is, never the masks themselves.
90	
91	| Key | What it holds |
92	| --- | --- |
93	| `mask_size` | The masks' own width and height. |
94	| `frames` | How many frames in the window have been analysed. |
95	| `subject_found` | Whether any frame holds a person. |
96	| `count` | How many runs there are. |
97	| `runs` | Each run of consecutive frames that agree, with `from`, `to`, `subject_found` and `frames`, in the file's own time. |
98	
99	A frame holds a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. `runs` have no `clip_time` or `timeline`, even with `clip`.
100	
101	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) draws these masks. A still picture's masks aren't this tool's. Use [`analyze_cutout`](#analyze_cutout) for those.
102	
103	### `kind: faces`
104	
105	Finds every face at 10 samples a second of the file's own time. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
106	
107	| Sample key | What it holds |
108	| --- | --- |
109	| `source` | The sample's instant in the file. |
110	| `frame` | The time of the frame it read, the first at or after `source` within one sample, or null. |
111	| `faces` | Each face in the sample. |
112	
113	| Face key | What it holds |
114	| --- | --- |
115	| `box` | `[x, y, w, h]`, from 0 to 1 of the upright picture, measured from its top-left corner. |
116	| `confidence` | How sure the detection is. |
117	| `roll`, `yaw` | How far the face is tilted and turned, in radians. |
118	| `mouth_gap` | The inner lips' height, over the face box's height. |
119	| `mouth_width` | The outer lips' width, over the face box's height. |
120	
121	`mouth_gap` over `mouth_width` is how open the mouth is. Values are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where no value was found.
122	
123	Faces are ordered from left to right and carry no identity or name. To follow one, follow its box from sample to sample.
124	
125	### `kind: subjects`
126	
127	Finds people and the regions the eye is drawn to, at 10 samples a second. Every sample instant is also a `faces` sample. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
128	
129	Each sample has `source` and `frame`, as `faces` does, then `people` and `salient`. Both are lists of `box` and `confidence`, with boxes measured as faces' are and ordered from left to right, with no identity. A person box covers the head and shoulders. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/).
130	
131	### `kind: sound_events`
132	
133	Listens to the file's first sound track with Apple's Sound Analysis, in windows of 1.5 s that start every 0.75 s, and says how sure it is of six kinds of sound: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It needs a file with sound, and an audio file works.
134	
135	| Key | What it holds |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| `window`, `hop` | The window's length and the step between windows, in ticks: 900,000 and 450,000. |
138	| `groups` | Each kind of sound, with `name`, `labels` (the classifier's labels it's the highest confidence of), `first_class` and `threshold`. |
139	| `count` | How many windows came back. |
140	| `windows` | Each window, with `source`, its start in the file, and a confidence from 0 to 1 for each of the six kinds. |
141	
142	Confidences are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where a window runs past the end of the sound.
143	
144	:::note
145	These are hints, never a finding on their own. `first_class` is false and `threshold` is null for all six.
146	:::
147	
148	## `analyze_cutout`
149	
150	Says where Remove Background stands for cut-out clips and makes their masks now. It's the agent's version of **Status** and [**Analyze Now**](/effects/remove-background/#analyze-now) in the Clip tab's **Picture ▸ Background** section.
151	
152	A cut-out clip is one whose `set_video` `cutout` is set, which is what **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the section's checkbox do. A clip's masks are made as soon as that's set, so an agent needs this tool only to wait for them or to read how they went. A still picture counts, and its one frame is made from the picture itself.
153	
154	A call asks for every frame the clips play and runs again an analysis that failed or was stopped. Frames already analysed are never analysed again. It then waits up to `wait` seconds for every clip to settle, and it never refuses for time: call again to keep waiting. The Assistant's **Stop** ends the wait.
155	
156	**Arguments**
157	
158	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
159	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
160	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The cut-out clips to answer for. Left out, every cut-out clip in the timeline or nest that's open, in timeline order. |
161	| `wait` | number | No | How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, from 0 to 60. Left out, it's 0, which answers now. |
162	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
163	
164	**What it answers**
165	
166	`clips`, a row for each clip, and the `project` summary. Each row has these keys:
167	
168	| Key | What it holds |
169	| --- | --- |
170	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
171	| `state` | Where it stands. See the next table. |
172	| `progress` | From 0 to 1. |
173	| `quality` | The clip's cutout quality, `standard` or `best`. |
174	| `frames` | How many frames of the file the clip plays, which is 1 for a picture. |
175	| `covered` | How many of those are analysed. |
176	| `ready` | Whether `covered` equals `frames`. |
177	| `subject_found` | Whether a subject was found. |
178	| `centroid` | `x` and `y`, the subject's mean centre over those frames, in the media's upright pixels from the top left with y going down. Null unless the state is `ready`. The app doesn't show this figure. |
179	| `error` | With `failed`, the sentence saying why. |
180	
181	| `state` | What it means | The app's **Status** |
182	| --- | --- | --- |
183	| `analyzing` | The masks are being made. | **Analyzing N %** |
184	| `ready` | Every frame is analysed, and a person, or a picture's foreground subject, was found. | **Ready** |
185	| `no_person` | Every frame is analysed and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. | **No person found** |
186	| `no_subject` | A picture with subject `foreground` has no subject, so it draws whole. | **No subject found** |
187	| `failed` | The masks couldn't be made. | **Failed:** and the reason |
188	| `no_picture` | The clip plays no frame of its file. | **No picture to analyze** |
189	
190	Every state but `analyzing` counts as settled.
191	
192	**When it refuses**
193	
194	Nothing is done when:
195	
196	- `wait` is outside 0 to 60: "wait must be from 0 to 60 seconds."
197	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
198	- A clip you named has no Remove Background: "Clip 3 has no Remove Background; set_video `{cutout: {}}` turns it on."
199	- With `clips` left out, no clip in the open timeline or nest has it on.
